content.thinking:
I'm envisioning a Genshin-style red panda balanced on a mossy stone — cel-shaded with gold filigree, tassels, and a soft Dendro-green elemental glow, sized realistically with a stocky body and long tail, trying to settle on a natural standing or hind-leg balancing pose.

Now I'm thinking through the skeleton structure, deciding on a stone roughly half a meter wide under the panda with its own joint, and working out whether the root joint should be the pelvis/hips or a separate base so the stone and animal animate correctly without unwanted coupling.

I'm also calculating proportions: stone top surface height, panda hip height sitting on it, body length, and tail reach, aiming for a total figure around 0.65 m tall with a balancing stance where front paws rest on the stone and the tail arches up as a counterweight.

For the pose itself, I'm settling on a diagonal balancing stance with the tail curved in an S-shape for counterbalance, forelegs slightly extended, and the head tilted forward. I'm sizing the stone elongated at roughly 0.6 x 0.42 m to match the panda's body proportions, and now I'm sketching the panda's cel-shaded color palette—rust-orange coat, cream facial markings, and white-tipped ears.

Now I'm adding dark brown-black legs and belly typical of a red panda, a ringed tail alternating rust and dark orange bands, and large emerald-green anime eyes to fit the Dendro theme. I'm layering in Genshin-style accents—a teal ribbon collar with a gold Dendro-leaf charm and tassels, plus glowing moss, spore motes, and small luminous sprouts on the stone—and starting to lay out the skeleton coordinates with the panda facing forward and hips rooted near the stone's center.

I'm working through a hunched spine chain from hips up through shoulders and neck to a wide, short-snouted head, then defining the hind leg segments (thigh, shin, flat sole) to capture the short, plantigrade stance characteristic of a red panda.

For the front legs, the target is the toe tip with the last segment pointing along the forward direction and the heel positioned 0.06 back from it; shoulder height is 0.45, giving a vertical reach of about 0.225 to solve against.

I realize the vertical drop of 0.225 exceeds my current segment lengths' total reach, so I need to either lengthen the segments to around [0.12, 0.11, 0.06] or lower the whole body — dropping hips to 0.40 and shoulders to 0.42 gives a more comfortable bend where thigh (0.11) and shin (0.10) sum close to the needed distance.

For the overall pose, I'm leaning toward a "balancing" feel — wide stance with paws spread outward (front ±0.13, hind ±0.12), tail arched, maybe even lifting one or both front paws slightly like the panda is balancing on something narrow, which feels more evocative and cute while still fitting the rest-pose guidelines.

Red pandas do stand upright on hind legs with arms out to balance, which is iconic, but that's too complex for this rig's proportions, so I'll stick with all-fours with arms spread, tail raised in an S-curve, and head tilted slightly up. I'm also thinking of adding a small detail like a glowing sprout or collar with tassels sitting on its head for character, and building the rock it stands on from flattened icospheres with mottled grey-blue stone coloring and green moss on top.

I'm cel-shading the stone with moss painted procedurally on upward-facing surfaces, adding grass tufts via textured cards, small flowers and mushrooms, and a glowing green Dendro-style rune decal on the stone's side for an ornate touch, plus a gold-trimmed tassel on the panda's collar. For fur detail I'll use spiky cream cards for cheek ruffs, ear tufts, and belly edge fur, all lit with proper frame normals to keep the toon-shaded look consistent. Now I'm moving into working out the actual geometry coordinates.

Still writing geometry...

Checking the dome profile at the edges, I worry paws might hover if the surface slopes down too much, so I'm flattening the top curve instead.

Now I'm thinking through the rock details -- small flattened icosahedron lumps resting on the floor, pebbles, moss mottling on upward-facing surfaces, draping moss clusters over the edges, and scattered moss tuft cards avoiding the spots where the panda's paws will rest.

For the panda body, I'm planning a loft along a spine chain: hips joint at the back, spine points curving up through the chest, then into a neck chain leading to a forward-aimed head joint, plus a separate tail chain branching backward from the hips and leg chains attached as well. I'm working out how the hips root joint and the first spine joint should share the same starting position so the chain connects cleanly.

Defining loft stations...

I should check the loft builder's signature to confirm the width/height per-point format works as expected. For the red panda's coloring, I want a cel-shaded countershade effect going from rust-red on the back to dark chestnut on the belly and legs.

Picking out actual red panda colors now—brighter rust-orange for the back, deep chestnut-black for the belly/legs, cream for highlights, and alternating rust/darker rust rings for the tail.

I'm working out the tail geometry: a sweep path curving upward from the hips in an S-shape for balance, tapering toward a dark tip, with eight alternating rings along its length to mimic the ringed pattern, using a periodic paint function based on position along the sweep.

That's too long for the panda body, so I'm scaling the tail curve down to a more proportional size, around 0.55 total length, recomputing the segment points along the arched question-mark shape.

Now I'm sizing the tail radii, bulging in the middle and tapering bushy at the tip, and checking the overall height stays reasonable against the head and ears. I'm placing the head center and neck joint, then setting up the cranium as a flattened sphere, before turning to the face details -- broad cheeks, short snout, white muzzle, dark nose, and tear-mark markings characteristic of a red panda.

I'm also deciding on the big anime-style eye decals, picking a green iris to tie into the elemental theme, debating whether to include brows (since red pandas naturally have white eyebrow patches) and keeping a soft blush tone for charm. Now I'm starting the skull sphere geometry and setting up its fur-edge shading transition from rust to cream based on position.

For the facial coloring, I'm mapping out where rust-orange gives way to white across the head—white cheeks, white muzzle, rust forehead with pale eyebrow patches—using position-based rules relative to the head center to create a zigzag-edged white patch that blends naturally into the front of the face.

For the darker tear-stripe markings running from eyes to mouth corners, I think it's cleaner to add them as separate decal strokes projected onto the head surface rather than folding them into the position-based paint function.

Now I'm planning the snout structure—cream-colored, with a dark rounded nose at the tip, and separating the mouth into upper and lower jaw parts connected by a joint. The upper snout sits as a rounded ellipsoid forward on the head, the lower jaw a smaller ellipsoid beneath it with a pink tongue, and I'm considering leaving the mouth very slightly open (around 6-8 degrees) to show a bit of pink and tiny fangs for a cuter rest pose.

Next I'm working out the ears—large rounded triangles on top of the head, tilted outward with rust-colored outer fur and white inner fur plus small tufts, positioning them symmetrically and orienting the extrusion so they face forward with a slight tilt.

I'm layering the ear structure with a rust outer shell and a cream inner face, adding white fur tufts along the rim, and considering a small gold ear cuff with a dangling jade tassel on one ear for extra charm, though a simple collar pendant might suffice instead. Now I'm moving on to designing the eye decals on the skull.

Placing them at specific angles and sizes for an exaggerated anime look, then working out cheek ruffs as scattered fur-tuft cards tinted cream using greyscale textures, and starting to plan rust spine tufts and a cream chest patch for the body fur.

Then I'm thinking through body-wide fur cards: around 120 rust-tinted tufts scattered along the sides with a backward lean for a fuzzy silhouette, colored by sampling the coat paint at each card root. For the legs, I'm planning dark brown stout limb sweeps with a gradient from rust near the thighs to dark brown lower down, based on vertical position.

For the forelegs I'm using a position-based edge threshold around the hip level to split orange upper arm from dark chocolate lower leg with a zigzag transition. For the paws, I'm sketching flattened ellipsoid feet with small toe capsules—four per paw, 16 joints total across all legs—each toe as a short single-joint chain tipped with tiny cream claws.

Thinking about anatomical accuracy versus budget: real red pandas have five toes, but five per paw across four paws pushes joint count higher (20 vs 16), so I'm weighing a stylized four-toe "mitten" look against the extra joints, landing on an overall skeleton estimate around 55 joints including spine, neck, ears, tail, legs, and toes. I'm now defining each leg's joint chain as hip, knee, heel/ankle, and toe tip to set up the limb geometry.

With 4 points and 3 spans, I settle on naming the joints hip, knee, ankle, then foot as the tip joint at the toe end, aimed along the end tangent. Now I'm working out the toe geometry attached to that foot joint.

I'll place the floor contact point under each foot at the sole position, then work out limb sweep radii—thicker at the thighs tapering down toward the paws, keeping the hind legs a bit thinner than the front.

I'm using a polyline through the limb joint points so the sweep skin rounds the corners naturally at each joint, with small pale claw spikes at the toes and a touch of darker fluffy fur at the wrists for texture. Now I'm sketching an ornate teal-green collar in the Genshin style.

Keeping two ribbon tails trailing down the chest. For a head ornament, I'm picturing a small glowing Dendro sprout between the ears—stem with two leaves—playing into a cute "balancing something on head" theme.

For stone surface details, I'm layering moss, small glowing flower clusters, a pair of glowing mushrooms with spotted caps, and a ring of tiny floating sparkle motes (diamond-shaped, green/gold glow) hovering above the panda. I'm also adding a decal of a Dendro glyph rune on the stone's side that glows, plus a thin gold scrollwork filigree band around the stone's base.

Thinking through the stone's gold inlay next -- a carved ring with gold-inlaid trim sweeping around its midsection, echoing Genshin ruin aesthetics, alongside the rune decal. For coloring, I'm planning a cel-shaded bluish-grey stone palette with moss patches painted procedurally on top using noise, where moss appears based on height and some randomized edge dripping for a natural look.

I'm also designing moss pillows as flattened green spheres along the rim, plus moss tufts and small flower decals (five petals, gold centers, pink/white tones) rendered as upright textured cards. Keeping an eye on part and triangle counts to stay efficient, and making sure the panda's paws properly contact the stone's mossy, painted top surface before I start writing the actual code.

I want to verify the builder's function signatures first -- things like loft options, part textures, and decals -- so I'll check the source for those definitions rather than relying on guesswork, then let the typechecker confirm correctness. Setting up the imports for geometry, math, paths, IK, paint, texture, and the toon/glow kits, and defining the color palette with rust, cream, chocolate browns, and nose tones for the character.

Finishing the palette with pink, gold, teal, jade, moss, and stone tones, then thinking through the flat color budget since paints are texture-based rather than counting against it. I'm setting up a cel-shaded fur paint using furEdge to split rust on the back from dark chocolate on the belly, mimicking a real red panda's darker underside, and considering adding cream shading to the body loft.

Now I'm working out the tail ring pattern, alternating rust and a lighter ring color with toothed zigzag edges to mimic real red panda tail markings, with a dark tip. Next I'm setting up the skull paint and head region definitions using head-local coordinates.

I need to figure out the joint chain from neck to head, placing neck1 and neck2 points before the head joint, oriented so its forward axis points outward for defining the skull's local coordinate frame.

Then I'm placing the skull as a sphere scaled into an ellipsoid using the head joint's local forward/up offsets, and considering adding cheek ruffs as flattened spheres or spiky cards for red panda-style facial fur.

Working through ear placement now, positioning them using local offsets on the head and figuring out the outline directions so the ear leans outward and slightly forward with its thickness along the correct axis.

I'll set the inner piece thickness to 0.008 and give the ears a slightly splayed, Genshin-style larger shape (0.075 height, 0.08 width), tied to hinge joints for earL/earR. For the inner ear coloring, I'll go with cream cel shading plus a darker rim line for definition.

For the outer ear I'm using a rust extrude with bevel, and a smaller cream inset shifted slightly forward. I'm adding fluffy cream tuft cards along the inner ear bottom, rigged to the nearest ear joint so they move rigidly with the ear. For the face, I'm placing a small glossy nose sphere with a tiny highlight at the muzzle tip, and considering thin ink sweeps for lip lines on the lower jaw if it needs to open.

For the facial markings, I'm designing an SVG decal covering tear lines, philtrum, and mouth details—tapering rust-brown tear marks from eyes to mouth corners, cream eyebrow dots, and small brown whisker dots on the muzzle—then projecting that decal forward onto the combined skull and muzzle surfaces.

Eyes need to sit above these marks with more lift to avoid z-fighting, so I'll give the marks a smaller lift value and the eyes a larger one, while keeping the tear-mark drawing clear of the actual eye sockets. I'm placing the eyes symmetrically on the skull ellipsoid at roughly ±36° azimuth with a slight elevation, working out their offset position from the head center.

For the iris I'm picking a green-teal tone that fits a cute red panda aesthetic rather than a realistic one. Then I'm sketching the muzzle as a small cream ellipsoid positioned forward and slightly down from the head center, sized to form a short snout, with separate upper muzzle and nose pieces layered on top.

Now I'm adding the lower jaw as a hinged cream ellipsoid that opens slightly, plus interior mouth details like a dark pink cavity and tongue, and tiny white fang cones top and bottom. For whiskers I'm planning thin rod sweeps—three per side, very short tubes—extending from the muzzle. Then I'm shifting to the body: lofting the main form, applying rust-colored fur cards for the back and haunches, and considering whether to add a lighter chest bib to match red panda coloring.

I'm now working out the leg joint structure—naming shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand for front legs and hip/knee/ankle/foot for hind legs, with left/right suffixes based on side sign. I'm deciding parent attachments so front legs hang from the upper spine joint and hind legs from the hip root, then setting foot placement coordinates for a wide, balanced stance relative to the body's width.

Now I'm figuring out the bend-hint directions for the IK chains: knees should hint forward and elbows should hint backward to get a natural quadruped pose, accounting for the fact that having a sole joint reduces the number of needed hint vectors by one.

Working through the hind leg geometry, I need to compute the heel position by offsetting from the toe target along the sole direction, then verify the root-to-heel distance stays within the thigh+shin reach given the hip position and stone surface height.

For the front legs, checking shoulder-to-heel distances against limb segment lengths confirms the forelimb stays nearly straight with only a slight elbow bend at this stance width, which is acceptable for a balancing pose with tail raised and head up. I'm now working out the thigh sweep radius values for the leg geometry.

Setting leg joint radii and then defining fur color transitions by height—rust coloring above a threshold y-level and chocolate below for both hind and front legs, with a teeth pattern marching along the leg's vertical sides.

Now I'm shaping the paws as slightly enlarged chocolate-toned ellipsoids beyond the leg radius, adding four small toe shapes with tiny curved cream-colored claw cones, keeping it simple without worrying about visible toe pads.

For bone assignment, I'll attach the paw ellipsoid and toes to the ankle joint since that's the last span joint before the foot tip, which makes sense since the ankle moves while the foot stays flat on the ground.

Now I'm building out four toes per foot with capsule shapes spreading from the ball of the foot, each with its own joint for digit articulation, plus small claw spikes at the toe tips, making sure everything lines up with the floor plane.

For the tail, I'm chaining five tapered spans off the hips with radii that bulge in the middle and narrow at the tip, painting a coat texture along its length, and adding a tuft of card geometry at the very end, keeping the root tucked just inside the body silhouette.

Now I'm scattering fur cards along the tail's outline for a fluffy look, then sprouting a small glowing leaf stem from the crown of the skull using a positioned offset above the head, and starting on a neck collar by looping a plane across the neck's first joint.

Still working out the loop geometry...

Now I'm adding ribbon tails hanging from the bow, then placing a gold pendant medallion at the front of the neck, trying to work out the exact surface coordinates for it.

I'm designing the pendant as a gold lathe disc with a glowing emerald center gem and a small tassel of capsule strands with teal fringe underneath, then moving on to shape the earring as a gold hoop ring.

I'll build the hoop as a small torus geometry positioned sideways at the lower earlobe, with a jade teardrop sphere hanging from it. For sparkle effects, I'm using four-point star card textures in gold, white, and green emissive colors, scattered and floating around the panda and stone using frame orientation at random positions.

Now I'm working out how these star cards should orient — standing vertical and facing along a random flow direction using a frame function, with cross:true to create crossing double-planes so they read from any viewing angle. I also want to keep the floating motes attached loosely near joints but capped below a certain height so they don't poke above the model's silhouette.

Then I move to the rock details: six icosahedron lumps with flattened shading, sunk slightly into the floor and scattered around the stone's radius. I'm writing a paint function that blends mossy and stony mottling based on surface normal and noise, deciding where moss grows versus bare stone...

I should predefine the stone and moss paint objects rather than recreating them each call to avoid waste. For moss texture I'm layering in small pillow-like sphere lumps around the top rim plus bright tufts, and for decoration I'm placing a glowing jade rune/leaf glyph on the stone's front-facing side so it's visible to viewers looking at the panda's front.

I'm placing small mushrooms near the stone's back-left base using a lathe-shaped cap with contrasting spotted decal coloring plus a swept stem, and scattering a few grass tufts and pebbles around the stone's base on the ground rather than adding a separate floor patch.

Now I'm sketching the texture SVGs: a tapered flame-leaf grass tuft shape with a subtle two-tone cel shading using a grey stripe for depth, and starting on a similar blade-tuft design with alternate coloring.

I'm planning the rest of the texture set too: a four-pointed gold star with a glowing white center, a stem-and-petal flower motif, a hanging gold fringe tassel, jade-colored rune glyphs drawn as thin strokes for decal use, facial marks, and a lathed medallion pendant with ridges, a jade gem, and a gold petal-ring decal layered on front.

I'm also sketching a small filigree plane decal—a gold ring-and-petal pattern over a teal disc—to place in front of the medallion, while deciding to skip a hanging bell on the tail. I'm mapping out the skeletal roles (tail, neck, spine, head, jaw) before moving to code, and I need to check how the loft builder handles station arrays and default cross-section shape before writing that part.
